monitor_alert_create_update_public_ip_ad.cli: az monitor activity-log alert create --resource-group '<resource group name>' --condition category=Administrative and operationName=Microsoft.Network/publicIPAddresses/write and level=<verbose | information | warning | error | critical>--scope '/subscriptions/<subscription ID>' --name '<activity log rule name>' -- subscription <subscription id> --action-group <action group ID> --location global

vm_jit_access_enabled.checkTitle: Enable Just-In-Time Access for Virtual Machines
vm_jit_access_enabled.recommendation: Enable Just-in-Time (JIT) network access for your Microsoft Azure virtual machines using the Azure Portal under Security Center > Just-in-time VM access.

vm_sufficient_daily_backup_retention_per.checkTitle: Ensure there is a sufficient daily backup retention period configured for Azure virtual machines.
vm_sufficient_daily_backup_retention_per.recommendation: Set the daily backup retention period for each VM's backup policy to meet or exceed your organization's minimum requirement.

vm_ensure_using_managed_disks.checkTitle: Ensure Virtual Machines are utilizing Managed Disks
vm_ensure_using_managed_disks.recommendation: 1. Using the search feature, go to Virtual Machines 2. Select the virtual machine you would like to convert 3. Select Disks in the menu for the VM 4. At the top select Migrate to managed disks 5. You may follow the prompts to convert the disk and finish by selecting Migrate to start the process

vm_ensure_using_approved_images.checkTitle: Ensure that Azure VMs are using an approved machine image.
vm_ensure_using_approved_images.recommendation: Re-create the required VM instances using the approved (golden) machine image.

vm_ensure_attached_disks_encrypted_with_.checkTitle: Ensure that 'OS and Data' disks are encrypted with Customer Managed Key (CMK)
vm_ensure_attached_disks_encrypted_with_.recommendation: Note: Disks must be detached from VMs to have encryption changed. 1. Go to Virtual machines 2. For each virtual machine, go to Settings 3. Click on Disks 4. Click the ellipsis (...), then click Detach to detach the disk from the VM 5. Now search for Disks and locate the unattached disk 6. Click the disk then select Encryption 7. Change your encryption type, then select your encryption set 8. Click Save 9. Go back to the VM and re-attach the disk

vm_trusted_launch_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Trusted Launch is enabled on Virtual Machines
vm_trusted_launch_enabled.recommendation: 1. Go to Virtual Machines 2. For each VM, under Settings, click on Configuration on the left blade 3. Under Security Type, select 'Trusted Launch Virtual Machines' 4. Make sure Enable Secure Boot & Enable vTPM are checked 5. Click on Apply.

vm_linux_enforce_ssh_authentication.checkTitle: Ensure SSH key authentication is enforced on Linux-based Virtual Machines
vm_linux_enforce_ssh_authentication.recommendation: Recreate Linux VMs with SSH key authentication enabled and password authentication disabled.

vm_scaleset_not_empty.checkTitle: Check for Empty Virtual Machine Scale Sets
vm_scaleset_not_empty.recommendation: Remove empty Azure virtual machine scale sets to optimize costs and simplify management.

vm_backup_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Backups are enabled for Azure Virtual Machines
vm_backup_enabled.recommendation: Enable Azure Backup for each VM by associating it with a Recovery Services vault and a backup policy.

vm_desired_sku_size.checkTitle: Ensure that your virtual machine instances are using SKU sizes that are approved by your organization
vm_desired_sku_size.recommendation: 1. Define and document your organization's approved VM SKU sizes based on workload requirements, cost constraints, and compliance needs. 2. Implement Azure Policy to enforce VM size restrictions across your subscriptions. 3. Use the 'Allowed virtual machine size SKUs' built-in policy to restrict VM creation to approved sizes. 4. Regularly review and update your approved SKU list based on changing business requirements and cost optimization goals. 5. Monitor VM usage and costs to ensure compliance with your SKU size policies.
vm_desired_sku_size.cli: az policy assignment create --display-name 'Allowed VM SKU Sizes' --policy cccc23c7-8427-4f53-ad12-b6a63eb452b3 -p '{"listOfAllowedSKUs": {"value": ["<desired-sku-1>", "<desired-sku-2>"]}}' --scope /subscriptions/<subscription-id>

vm_scaleset_associated_with_load_balance.checkTitle: VM Scale Set Is Associated With Load Balancer
vm_scaleset_associated_with_load_balance.recommendation: Attach a load balancer to your Azure virtual machine scale set to ensure high availability and optimal traffic distribution.

vm_ensure_unattached_disks_encrypted_wit.checkTitle: Ensure that 'Unattached disks' are encrypted with 'Customer Managed Key' (CMK)
vm_ensure_unattached_disks_encrypted_wit.recommendation: If data stored in the disk is no longer useful, refer to Azure documentation to delete unattached data disks at: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/compute/disks/delete?view=rest-compute-2023-10-02&tabs=HTTP

aisearch_service_not_publicly_accessible.checkTitle: AI Search service has public network access disabled
aisearch_service_not_publicly_accessible.recommendation: Set `Public network access: Disabled`. Prefer **Private Link** and restrict any residual exposure to specific sources only. Use **least privilege** with Microsoft Entra ID RBAC instead of keys. Apply **defense in depth** with IP rules/trusted services, enable logs, and review access lists regularly.
aisearch_service_not_publicly_accessible.terraform:
```hcl
# Disable public network access for Azure AI Search
resource "azurerm_search_service" "<example_resource_name>" {
  name                = "<example_resource_name>"
  resource_group_name = "<example_resource_name>"
  location            = "<location>"
  sku                 = "basic"

  public_network_access_enabled = false  # CRITICAL: Disables public access to pass the check
}
```
aisearch_service_not_publicly_accessible.other:
1. In the Azure portal, open your AI Search service
2. Go to Settings > Networking
3. Under Public network access, select Disabled
4. Click Save
5. Wait a few minutes and re-run the check

postgresql_flexible_server_log_checkpoin.checkTitle: PostgreSQL Flexible Server has checkpoint logging enabled
postgresql_flexible_server_log_checkpoin.recommendation: Enable `log_checkpoints=on` and send logs to centralized, tamper-resistant storage. Monitor checkpoint frequency and failures with alerts. Apply **least privilege** to log access and set retention to support forensics as part of a **defense-in-depth** logging strategy.
postgresql_flexible_server_log_checkpoin.cli: az postgres flexible-server parameter set --resource-group <resourceGroupName> --server-name <serverName> --name log_checkpoints --value ON
postgresql_flexible_server_log_checkpoin.terraform:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_configuration" "<example_resource_name>" {
  name      = "log_checkpoints"
  server_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  
  value = "ON" # CRITICAL: enables checkpoint logging to pass the check
}
```
postgresql_flexible_server_log_checkpoin.other:
1. In the Azure portal, open your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
2. Go to Settings > Server parameters
3. Search for "log_checkpoints"
4. Set the value to ON
5. Click Save

postgresql_flexible_server_entra_id_auth.checkTitle: Microsoft Entra ID authentication is enabled for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
postgresql_flexible_server_entra_id_auth.recommendation: Federate PostgreSQL Flexible Server access through **Microsoft Entra ID** so MFA, conditional access, and centralized RBAC govern logins. Maintain at least one delegated administrator group and rotate membership through identity governance processes.
postgresql_flexible_server_entra_id_auth.cli:
az postgres flexible-server update --resource-group <resourceGroupName> --name <serverName> --active-directory-auth Enabled
az postgres flexible-server ad-admin create --resource-group <resourceGroupName> --server-name <serverName> --object-id <objectId> --display-name <displayName> --type User
postgresql_flexible_server_entra_id_auth.terraform:
```hcl
data "azurerm_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "example" {
  name                = "pg-flex"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  sku_name            = "GP_Standard_D4s_v3"
  administrator_login = "pgadmin"
  administrator_password = "<complexPassword>"
  storage_mb          = 131072
  version             = "16"

  authentication {
    active_directory_auth_enabled = true
    tenant_id                     = data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id
  }
}

resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_active_directory_administrator" "entra_admin" {
  server_id     = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.example.id
  object_id     = var.entra_object_id
  principal_name = var.entra_principal_name
  principal_type = "User"
  tenant_id     = data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id
}
```
postgresql_flexible_server_entra_id_auth.other:
1. In the Azure Portal, open Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server and select the target server.
2. Under Security > Authentication, set Microsoft Entra ID authentication (or combined mode) to Enabled and save the change.
3. Under Security > Microsoft Entra ID, add at least one administrator (user or group) linked to an Entra object ID and confirm the assignment.

postgresql_flexible_server_log_connectio.checkTitle: PostgreSQL flexible server has log_connections enabled
postgresql_flexible_server_log_connectio.recommendation: Set `log_connections` to `ON` and integrate logs with centralized monitoring. Define retention and alerts for abnormal patterns. Combine with **least privilege**, strong authentication, and network restrictions to deliver **defense in depth** and prevent unauthorized access.
postgresql_flexible_server_log_connectio.other:
1. Sign in to the Azure portal
2. Go to: Azure Database for PostgreSQL > Flexible servers > select <example_resource_name>
3. Under Settings, open Server parameters and search for "log_connections"
4. Confirm the parameter shows Value: ON and is Read-only (no change required)

postgresql_flexible_server_connection_th.checkTitle: Flexible PostgreSQL server has connection_throttling enabled
postgresql_flexible_server_connection_th.recommendation:
Enable `connection_throttling` and align connection limits with expected load.

Apply **defense in depth**: use connection pooling, exponential backoff, and alerts on connection spikes; prefer private access and restrictive networking to reduce exposure.
postgresql_flexible_server_connection_th.cli: az postgres flexible-server parameter set --resource-group <resourceGroupName> --server-name <serverName> --name connection_throttle.enable --value on
postgresql_flexible_server_connection_th.terraform:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_configuration" "<example_resource_name>" {
  name      = "connection_throttle.enable"
  server_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  value     = "on" # CRITICAL: Enables connection_throttle.enable to pass the check
}
```
postgresql_flexible_server_connection_th.other:
1. Sign in to Azure Portal and go to Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible servers
2. Select the target server
3. In Settings, click Server parameters
4. Search for connection_throttle.enable
5. Set the value to ON and click Save

postgresql_flexible_server_enforce_ssl_e.checkTitle: PostgreSQL Flexible Server enforces SSL connections
postgresql_flexible_server_enforce_ssl_e.recommendation: Enforce encryption in transit: set `require_secure_transport=ON`, prefer **TLS 1.3** (or at least `ssl_min_protocol_version=1.2`), and require clients to verify server identity. Disable mixed modes, rotate certificates, and restrict access via **private endpoints** to apply **defense in depth**.
postgresql_flexible_server_enforce_ssl_e.cli: az postgres flexible-server parameter set --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --server-name <SERVER_NAME> --name require_secure_transport --value ON
postgresql_flexible_server_enforce_ssl_e.terraform:
```hcl
# Enable SSL/TLS enforcement on a PostgreSQL Flexible Server
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_configuration" "<example_resource_name>" {
  name      = "require_secure_transport"   # CRITICAL: Target the SSL enforcement parameter
  server_id = "<example_resource_id>"      # ID of the target flexible server
  value     = "ON"                          # CRITICAL: Enforce SSL/TLS
}
```
postgresql_flexible_server_enforce_ssl_e.other:
1. Sign in to the Azure portal
2. Go to: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server > your server
3. Select Server parameters
4. Search for require_secure_transport
5. Set it to ON
6. Click Save

postgresql_flexible_server_log_retention.checkTitle: PostgreSQL flexible server log_retention_days is between 4 and 7 days
postgresql_flexible_server_log_retention.recommendation: Set `log_retention_days` to `4-7` to balance visibility and exposure. Export logs to centralized SIEM or secure storage for longer retention and analysis. Enforce **least privilege**, encryption, and immutability on log data, and monitor for gaps. Apply **defense in depth** with alerts on anomalous queries and failed logins.
postgresql_flexible_server_log_retention.cli: az postgres flexible-server parameter set --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --server-name <SERVER_NAME> --name logfiles.retention_days --value 7
postgresql_flexible_server_log_retention.terraform:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_configuration" "<example_resource_name>" {
  server_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name      = "logfiles.retention_days"
  value     = "7" # Critical: sets retention within 4-7 to pass the check
}
```
postgresql_flexible_server_log_retention.other:
1. In Azure Portal, go to Azure Database for PostgreSQL > Flexible servers and open your server
2. Select Server parameters
3. Search for logfiles.retention_days
4. Set the value to a number between 4 and 7 (e.g., 7)
5. Click Save

postgresql_flexible_server_allow_access_.checkTitle: PostgreSQL flexible server has 'Allow public access from any Azure service' disabled
postgresql_flexible_server_allow_access_.recommendation:
Remove the `0.0.0.0` rule and apply **least privilege**:
- Use **Private Endpoints** for access

- Isolate with VNET rules and NSGs
- Enforce TLS and strong authentication
- Monitor connection logs for anomalies

```hcl
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_firewall_rule" "<example_resource_name>" {
```

postgresql_flexible_server_allow_access_.other:

postgresql_flexible_server_log_disconnec.checkTitle: PostgreSQL Flexible Server has disconnection logging enabled
postgresql_flexible_server_log_disconnec.recommendation: Enable `log_disconnections` on all Flexible Servers. Complement with `log_connections` and appropriate duration/statement logging, centralize and retain logs, and alert on abnormal connect/disconnect patterns. Restrict log access. This enforces **accountability**, supports **defense in depth**, and speeds incident response.
postgresql_flexible_server_log_disconnec.cli: az postgres flexible-server parameter set --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --server-name <SERVER_NAME> --name log_disconnections --value on
postgresql_flexible_server_log_disconnec.terraform:

```hcl
# Enable log_disconnections on a PostgreSQL Flexible Server
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_configuration" "log_disconnections" {
  server_id = "<example_resource_id>"
  name      = "log_disconnections"
  value     = "on" # Critical: turns log_disconnections ON to pass the check
}
```
postgresql_flexible_server_log_disconnec.other:
1. In Azure Portal, go to Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible servers
2. Select your server
3. Under Settings, open Server parameters
4. Search for log_disconnections
5. Set it to ON
6. Click Save

compute_instance_security_groups_attache.checkTitle: Compute instances have security groups attached
compute_instance_security_groups_attache.recommendation:
Apply **defense-in-depth** for network security:
- Attach **security groups** to all instances; never deploy without firewall rules
- Follow **least privilege**: allow only required ports and sources; deny all by default
- Use **separate security groups** per tier (web, app, database) with explicit rules
- Avoid overly permissive rules like `0.0.0.0/0` ingress on sensitive ports
- Implement **network segmentation** with isolated networks or VLANs
- Enable **flow logs** for traffic analysis and anomaly detection
- Regularly **audit** security group rules and remove stale or overly broad permissions
compute_instance_security_groups_attache.terraform:
```hcl
# Terraform: ensure compute instance has security groups attached
resource "openstack_compute_instance_v2" "instance" {
  name            = "example-instance"
  image_id        = var.image_id
  flavor_id       = var.flavor_id
  key_pair        = var.key_pair_name
  # Critical: attach at least one security group
  security_groups = ["default", "web-sg", "app-sg"]

  network {
    name = var.network_name
  }
}
```
compute_instance_security_groups_attache.other:
1. Access the Horizon dashboard
2. Navigate to **Compute > Instances**
3. Locate instances without security groups (check the Security Groups column)
4. Select the instance, then **Actions > Edit Security Groups**
5. Add at least one security group (e.g., `default` or a custom group with least-privilege rules)
6. Click **Save** and verify the attachment
7. Test connectivity to ensure proper ingress/egress rules

apikeys_key_rotated_in_90_days.checkTitle: Ensure API Keys Are Rotated Every 90 Days
apikeys_key_rotated_in_90_days.recommendation: Ensure that all your Google Cloud API keys are regularly regenerated (rotated) in order to meet security and compliance requirements. By default, it is recommended to rotate keys every 90 days. Google Cloud Platform (GCP) API keys are simple, encrypted strings that can be used when calling specific APIs that don't need to access private user data. API keys are typically used to track API requests associated with your GCP project for quota and billing. Rotating GCP API keys will substantially reduce the window of opportunity for exploits and ensure that data can't be accessed with an outdated key that might have been lost, cracked, or stolen.

apikeys_api_restrictions_configured.checkTitle: Ensure API Keys Are Restricted to Only APIs That Application Needs Access
apikeys_api_restrictions_configured.recommendation: Ensure that the usage of your Google Cloud API keys is restricted to specific APIs such as Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) API, Cloud Storage API, Cloud Monitoring API and/or Cloud Logging API. All Google Cloud API keys that are being used for production applications should use API restrictions. In order to follow cloud security best practices and reduce the attack surface, Google Cloud API keys should be restricted to call only those APIs required by your application.

apikeys_key_exists.checkTitle: Ensure API Keys Only Exist for Active Services
apikeys_key_exists.recommendation: To avoid the security risk in using API keys, it is recommended to use standard authentication flow instead.

artifacts_container_analysis_enabled.checkTitle: GCP project has Artifact Registry Container Analysis API enabled
artifacts_container_analysis_enabled.recommendation: Enable **Artifact Analysis** (`containeranalysis.googleapis.com`) for projects hosting container images. Integrate scan results into CI/CD policy gates, apply **least privilege** to findings access, and rebuild images promptly to maintain **defense in depth**.
artifacts_container_analysis_enabled.other:
1. In Google Cloud Console, ensure the correct project is selected
2. Go to APIs & Services > Library
3. Search for "Container Analysis API"
4. Click the API, then click "Enable"

cloudstorage_bucket_public_access.checkTitle: Ensure That Cloud Storage Bucket Is Not Anonymously or Publicly Accessible
cloudstorage_bucket_public_access.recommendation: It is recommended that IAM policy on Cloud Storage bucket does not allows anonymous or public access.

cloudstorage_bucket_uniform_bucket_level.checkTitle: Ensure That Cloud Storage Buckets Have Uniform Bucket-Level Access Enabled
cloudstorage_bucket_uniform_bucket_level.recommendation: It is recommended that uniform bucket-level access is enabled on Cloud Storage buckets.

cloudstorage_bucket_log_retention_policy.checkTitle: Cloud Storage log bucket has a Retention Policy with Bucket Lock enabled
cloudstorage_bucket_log_retention_policy.recommendation: Configure a retention policy and enable Bucket Lock on all Cloud Storage buckets used as log sinks to ensure log integrity and immutability.
cloudstorage_bucket_log_retention_policy.other:
1) Open Google Cloud Console → Storage → Buckets → <LOG_BUCKET_NAME>
2) Go to the **Configuration** tab
3) Under **Retention policy**, ensure a retention duration is set
4) Click **Lock** to enable Bucket Lock and confirm the operation

cloudstorage_audit_logs_enabled.checkTitle: Data Access audit logs are enabled for Cloud Storage
cloudstorage_audit_logs_enabled.recommendation: Enable Data Access audit logs (DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE) for Cloud Storage at the project level to track all read and write operations on storage objects for security monitoring and compliance.
cloudstorage_audit_logs_enabled.other:
1) Console → IAM & Admin → Audit Logs
2) Find 'Google Cloud Storage' in the list of services
3) Check the boxes for 'Data Read' and 'Data Write'
4) Click 'Save' to apply the configuration

Note: This is a project-level setting that applies to all Cloud Storage buckets in the project.

cloudstorage_uses_vpc_service_controls.checkTitle: Cloud Storage services are protected by VPC Service Controls
cloudstorage_uses_vpc_service_controls.recommendation: Enable VPC Service Controls for all Cloud Storage buckets by adding their projects to a service perimeter with storage.googleapis.com as a restricted service. This prevents data exfiltration and ensures API calls are only allowed from authorized networks.
cloudstorage_uses_vpc_service_controls.other:
1) Open Google Cloud Console → Security → VPC Service Controls
2) Create a new service perimeter or select an existing one
3) Add the relevant GCP projects to the perimeter's protected resources
4) Add 'storage.googleapis.com' to the list of restricted services
5) Configure appropriate ingress and egress rules
6) Save the perimeter configuration

cloudstorage_bucket_versioning_enabled.checkTitle: Cloud Storage buckets have Object Versioning enabled
cloudstorage_bucket_versioning_enabled.recommendation: Enable Object Versioning on Cloud Storage buckets to preserve previous object versions and improve data recoverability and auditability.
cloudstorage_bucket_versioning_enabled.other:
1) Open Google Cloud Console → Storage → Buckets → <BUCKET_NAME>
2) Tab 'Configuration'
3) Under 'Object versioning', click 'Enable Object Versioning'
4) Save changes

cloudstorage_bucket_lifecycle_management.checkTitle: Cloud Storage buckets have lifecycle management enabled
cloudstorage_bucket_lifecycle_management.recommendation: Configure lifecycle rules to automatically delete stale objects or transition them to colder storage classes according to your organization's retention and cost-optimization policy.
cloudstorage_bucket_lifecycle_management.other:
1) Open Google Cloud Console → Storage → Buckets → <BUCKET_NAME>
2) Tab 'Lifecycle'
3) Add rule(s) to delete or transition objects (e.g., delete after 365 days; transition STANDARD→NEARLINE after 90 days)
4) Save

cloudstorage_bucket_soft_delete_enabled.checkTitle: Cloud Storage buckets have Soft Delete enabled
cloudstorage_bucket_soft_delete_enabled.recommendation: Enable Soft Delete on Cloud Storage buckets to retain deleted objects for a defined period, improving data recoverability and resilience against accidental or malicious deletions.
cloudstorage_bucket_soft_delete_enabled.other:
1) Open Google Cloud Console → Storage → Buckets → <BUCKET_NAME>
2) Tab 'Configuration'
3) Under 'Soft Delete', click 'Enable Soft Delete'
4) Set the desired retention duration and save changes

cloudstorage_bucket_logging_enabled.checkTitle: Cloud Storage buckets have Usage and Storage Logs enabled
cloudstorage_bucket_logging_enabled.recommendation: Enable Usage and Storage Logs for all Cloud Storage buckets to track access, detect anomalies, and maintain audit visibility of data operations.
cloudstorage_bucket_logging_enabled.cli: gsutil logging set on -b gs://<LOGGING_BUCKET> -o <LOG_OBJECT_PREFIX> gs://<BUCKET_NAME>

cloudstorage_bucket_sufficient_retention.checkTitle: Cloud Storage bucket has a sufficient Retention Policy period
cloudstorage_bucket_sufficient_retention.recommendation: Define and apply a bucket-level Retention Policy that meets your minimum retention requirement (e.g., 90 or 365 days) to enforce data recoverability and compliance.
cloudstorage_bucket_sufficient_retention.other:
1) Console → Storage → Buckets → <BUCKET_NAME>
2) Tab 'Configuration' → 'Retention policy'
3) Set the required retention period (e.g., 90 or 365 days) and save
4) (Optional) Lock the policy if required by compliance

gke_cluster_no_default_service_account.checkTitle: Ensure GKE clusters are not running using the Compute Engine default service account
gke_cluster_no_default_service_account.recommendation: Create and use minimally privileged service accounts for GKE cluster nodes instead of using the Compute Engine default service account.

dataproc_encrypted_with_cmks_disabled.checkTitle: Ensure that Dataproc Cluster is encrypted using Customer-Managed Encryption Key
dataproc_encrypted_with_cmks_disabled.recommendation: Ensure that your Google Cloud Dataproc clusters on Compute Engine are encrypted with Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) in order to control the cluster data encryption/decryption process. You can create and manage your own Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) with Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS). Cloud KMS provides secure and efficient encryption key management, controlled key rotation, and revocation mechanisms.

cloudsql_instance_mysql_local_infile_fla.checkTitle: Ensure That the Local_infile Database Flag for a Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Is Set to Off
cloudsql_instance_mysql_local_infile_fla.recommendation: It is recommended to set the local_infile database flag for a Cloud SQL MySQL instance to off.
cloudsql_instance_mysql_local_infile_fla.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags local_infile=off

cloudsql_instance_postgres_enable_pgaudi.checkTitle: Ensure That 'cloudsql.enable_pgaudit' Database Flag for each Cloud Sql Postgresql Instance Is Set to 'on' For Centralized Logging
cloudsql_instance_postgres_enable_pgaudi.recommendation: As numerous other recommendations in this section consist of turning on flags for logging purposes, your organization will need a way to manage these logs. You may have a solution already in place. If you do not, consider installing and enabling the open source pgaudit extension within PostgreSQL and enabling its corresponding flag of cloudsql.enable_pgaudit. This flag and installing the extension enables database auditing in PostgreSQL through the open-source pgAudit extension. This extension provides detailed session and object logging to comply with government, financial, & ISO standards and provides auditing capabilities to mitigate threats by monitoring security events on the instance. Enabling the flag and settings later in this recommendation will send these logs to Google Logs Explorer so that you can access them in a central location.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_enable_pgaudi.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags cloudsql.enable_pgaudit=On

cloudsql_instance_ssl_connections.checkTitle: Ensure That the Cloud SQL Database Instance Requires All Incoming Connections To Use SSL
cloudsql_instance_ssl_connections.recommendation: It is recommended to enforce all incoming connections to SQL database instance to use SSL.

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_trace_flag.checkTitle: Ensure '3625 (trace flag)' database flag for all Cloud SQL Server instances is set to 'on'
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_trace_flag.recommendation: It is recommended to set 3625 (trace flag) database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance to on.

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_statement.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log_statement Database Flag for Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set Appropriately
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_statement.recommendation: The value ddl logs all data definition statements. A value of 'ddl' is recommended unless otherwise directed by your organization's logging policy.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_statement.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_statement=ddl

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_user_options.checkTitle: Ensure 'user options' database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance is not configured
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_user_options.recommendation: It is recommended that, user options database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance should not be configured.

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_disconnec.checkTitle: Ensure That the log_disconnections Database Flag for Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set to On
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_disconnec.recommendation: Enabling the log_disconnections setting logs the end of each session, including the session duration.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_disconnec.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_disconnections=on

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_connectio.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log_connections Database Flag for Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set to On
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_connectio.recommendation: PostgreSQL does not log attempted connections by default. Enabling the log_connections setting will create log entries for each attempted connection as well as successful completion of client authentication which can be useful in troubleshooting issues and to determine any unusual connection attempts to the server.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_connectio.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_connections=on

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_user_connect.checkTitle: Ensure 'user Connections' Database Flag for Cloud Sql Sql Server Instance Is Set to a Non-limiting Value
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_user_connect.recommendation: It is recommended to check the user connections for a Cloud SQL SQL Server instance to ensure that it is not artificially limiting connections.
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_user_connect.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags user connections=0

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_error_ver.checkTitle: Ensure Log_error_verbosity Database Flag for Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set to DEFAULT or Stricter
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_error_ver.recommendation: Auditing helps in troubleshooting operational problems and also permits forensic analysis. If log_error_verbosity is not set to the correct value, too many details or too few details may be logged. This flag should be configured with a value of 'DEFAULT' or stricter. This recommendation is applicable to PostgreSQL database instances.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_error_ver.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_error_verbosity=default

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_contained_da.checkTitle: Ensure that the 'contained database authentication' database flag for Cloud SQL on the SQL Server instance is set to 'off'
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_contained_da.recommendation: It is recommended to set contained database authentication database flag for Cloud SQL on the SQL Server instance to off.
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_contained_da.cli: gcloud sql instances patch <INSTANCE_NAME> --database-flags contained database authentication=off

cloudsql_instance_public_ip.checkTitle: Check for Cloud SQL Database Instances with Public IPs
cloudsql_instance_public_ip.recommendation: To lower the organization's attack surface, Cloud SQL databases should not have public IPs. Private IPs provide improved network security and lower latency for your application.

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_external_scr.checkTitle: Ensure 'external scripts enabled' database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance is set to 'off'
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_external_scr.recommendation: It is recommended to set external scripts enabled database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance to off
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_external_scr.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags external scripts enabled=off

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_error.checkTitle: Ensure that the Log_min_error_statement Flag for a Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set Appropriately
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_error.recommendation: Auditing helps in troubleshooting operational problems and also permits forensic analysis. If log_min_error_statement is not set to the correct value, messages may not be classified as error messages appropriately. Considering general log messages as error messages would make is difficult to find actual errors and considering only stricter severity levels as error messages may skip actual errors to log their SQL statements. The log_min_error_statement flag should be set to ERROR or stricter.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_error.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_min_error_statement=error

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_messa.checkTitle: Ensure that the Log_min_messages Flag for a Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set Appropriately
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_messa.recommendation: The log_min_messages flag defines the minimum message severity level that is considered as an error statement. Messages for error statements are logged with the SQL statement. Valid values include DEBUG5, DEBUG4, DEBUG3, DEBUG2, DEBUG1, INFO, NOTICE, WARNING, ERROR, LOG, FATAL, and PANIC. Each severity level includes the subsequent levels mentioned above. ERROR is considered the best practice setting. Changes should only be made in accordance with the organization's logging policy.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_messa.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_min_messages=warning

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_cross_db_own.checkTitle: Ensure that the 'cross db ownership chaining' database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance is set to 'off'
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_cross_db_own.recommendation: It is recommended to set cross db ownership chaining database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance to off.
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_cross_db_own.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags cross db ownership=off

cloudsql_instance_private_ip_assignment.checkTitle: Ensure Instance IP assignment is set to private
cloudsql_instance_private_ip_assignment.recommendation: Setting databases access only to private will reduce attack surface.

cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_durat.checkTitle: Ensure that the Log_min_duration_statement Flag for a Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Instance Is Set to -1
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_durat.recommendation: Logging SQL statements may include sensitive information that should not be recorded in logs. This recommendation is applicable to PostgreSQL database instances.
cloudsql_instance_postgres_log_min_durat.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags log_min_duration_statement=-1

cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_remote_acces.checkTitle: Ensure 'remote access' database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance is set to 'off'
cloudsql_instance_sqlserver_remote_acces.recommendation: It is recommended to set remote access database flag for Cloud SQL SQL Server instance to off.

cloudsql_instance_mysql_skip_show_databa.checkTitle: Ensure Skip_show_database Database Flag for Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Is Set to On
cloudsql_instance_mysql_skip_show_databa.recommendation: It is recommended to set skip_show_database database flag for Cloud SQL Mysql instance to on.
cloudsql_instance_mysql_skip_show_databa.cli: gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME --database-flags skip_show_database=on

cloudsql_instance_automated_backups.checkTitle: Ensure That Cloud SQL Database Instances Are Configured With Automated Backups
cloudsql_instance_automated_backups.recommendation: It is recommended to have all SQL database instances set to enable automated backups.

cloudsql_instance_public_access.checkTitle: Ensure That Cloud SQL Database Instances Do Not Implicitly Whitelist All Public IP Addresses
cloudsql_instance_public_access.recommendation: Database Server should accept connections only from trusted Network(s)/IP(s) and restrict access from public IP addresses.

bigquery_table_cmk_encryption.checkTitle: Ensure BigQuery tables are encrypted with Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs).
bigquery_table_cmk_encryption.recommendation: Encrypting tables with Cloud KMS Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) will allow for a more granular control over data encryption/decryption process.

bigquery_dataset_public_access.checkTitle: Ensure That BigQuery Datasets Are Not Anonymously or Publicly Accessible.
bigquery_dataset_public_access.recommendation: It is recommended that the IAM policy on BigQuery datasets does not allow anonymous and/or public access.

bigquery_dataset_cmk_encryption.checkTitle: Ensure BigQuery datasets are encrypted with Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs).
bigquery_dataset_cmk_encryption.recommendation: Encrypting datasets with Cloud KMS Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) will allow for a more granular control over data encryption/decryption process.

gcr_container_scanning_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Image Vulnerability Scanning using GCR Container Scanning or a third-party provider
gcr_container_scanning_enabled.recommendation: Enable vulnerability scanning for images stored in GCR using GCR Container Scanning or a third-party provider.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for Audit Configuration Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: By using Google Cloud alerting policies to detect audit configuration changes, you make sure that the recommended state of audit configuration is well maintained so that all the activities performed within your GCP project are available for security analysis and auditing at any point in time.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for Project Ownership Assignments/Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: Using Google Cloud alerting policies to detect ownership assignments/changes will help you maintain the right access permissions for each IAM member created within your project, follow the security principle of least privilege, and prevent any accidental or intentional changes that may lead to unauthorized actions.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for SQL Instance Configuration Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for SQL instance configuration changes.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for Custom Role Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for changes to Identity and Access Management (IAM) role creation, deletion and updating activities.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for VPC Network Route Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network route changes.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Compute Engine configuration changes are monitored with log metric filters and alerts
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: Configure log-based metric filters to detect Compute Engine configuration changes and create alert policies that trigger notifications when these metrics increment. Apply the **principle of least privilege** to limit who can modify compute resources, and establish **change management processes** to review and approve infrastructure modifications.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.cli: gcloud logging metrics create compute_config_changes --description="Compute Engine configuration changes" --log-filter='protoPayload.serviceName="compute.googleapis.com"' && gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --notification-channels=CHANNEL_ID --display-name="Compute Engine Configuration Changes Alert" --condition-threshold-value=1 --condition-threshold-duration=0s --condition-filter='metric.type="logging.googleapis.com/user/compute_config_changes"'
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.other:
1. Open the Google Cloud Console
2. Navigate to Logging > Logs-based Metrics
3. Click 'Create Metric'
4. Set Metric Type to 'Counter'
5. Enter filter: protoPayload.serviceName="compute.googleapis.com"
6. Click 'Create Metric'
7. Navigate to Monitoring > Alerting
8. Click 'Create Policy'
9. Click 'Add Condition'
10. Select your log metric in the metric dropdown
11. Set threshold and conditions
12. Add notification channels
13. Click 'Save'

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for VPC Network Firewall Rule Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Network Firewall rule changes.

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for VPC Network Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network changes.

logging_sink_created.checkTitle: Ensure there is at least one sink used to export copies of all the log entries.
logging_sink_created.recommendation: It is recommended to create a sink that will export copies of all the log entries. This can help aggregate logs from multiple projects and export them to a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).

logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.checkTitle: Ensure That the Log Metric Filter and Alerts Exist for Cloud Storage IAM Permission Changes.
logging_log_metric_filter_and_alert_for_.recommendation: It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for Cloud Storage Bucket IAM changes.

dns_dnssec_disabled.checkTitle: Ensure That DNSSEC Is Enabled for Cloud DNS
dns_dnssec_disabled.recommendation: Ensure that DNSSEC security feature is enabled for all your Google Cloud DNS managed zones in order to protect your domains against spoofing and cache poisoning attacks. By default, DNSSEC is not enabled for Google Cloud public DNS managed zones. DNSSEC security feature helps mitigate the risk of such attacks by encrypting signing DNS records. As a result, it prevents attackers from issuing fake DNS responses that may misdirect web clients to fake, fraudulent or scam websites.

dns_rsasha1_in_use_to_key_sign_in_dnssec.checkTitle: Ensure That RSASHA1 Is Not Used for the Key-Signing Key in Cloud DNS DNSSEC
dns_rsasha1_in_use_to_key_sign_in_dnssec.recommendation: Ensure that Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) feature is not using the deprecated RSASHA1 algorithm for the Key-Signing Key (KSK) associated with your DNS managed zone file. The algorithm used for DNSSEC signing should be a strong one, such as ECDSAP256SHA256 algorithm, as this is secure and widely deployed, and therefore it is a good choice for both DNSSEC validation and signing.

dns_rsasha1_in_use_to_zone_sign_in_dnsse.checkTitle: Ensure That RSASHA1 Is Not Used for the Zone-Signing Key in Cloud DNS DNSSEC
dns_rsasha1_in_use_to_zone_sign_in_dnsse.recommendation: Ensure that Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) feature is not using the deprecated RSASHA1 algorithm for the Zone-Signing Key (ZSK) associated with your public DNS managed zone. The algorithm used for DNSSEC signing should be a strong one, such as RSASHA256, as this algorithm is secure and widely deployed, and therefore it is a good candidate for both DNSSEC validation and signing.

iam_audit_logs_enabled.checkTitle: Configure Google Cloud Audit Logs to Track All Activities
iam_audit_logs_enabled.recommendation: It is recommended that Cloud Audit Logging is configured to track all admin activities and read, write access to user data.

iam_sa_no_administrative_privileges.checkTitle: Ensure Service Account does not have admin privileges
iam_sa_no_administrative_privileges.recommendation: Ensure that your Google Cloud user-managed service accounts are not using privileged (administrator) roles, in order to implement the principle of least privilege and prevent any accidental or intentional modifications that may lead to data leaks and/or data loss.

iam_role_sa_enforce_separation_of_duties.checkTitle: Enforce Separation of Duties for Service-Account Related Roles
iam_role_sa_enforce_separation_of_duties.recommendation: Ensure that separation of duties (also known as segregation of duties - SoD) is enforced for all Google Cloud Platform (GCP) service-account related roles. The security principle of separation of duties has as its primary objective the prevention of fraud and human error. This objective is achieved by disbanding the tasks and associated privileges for a specific business process among multiple users/members. To follow security best practices, your GCP service accounts should not have the Service Account Admin and Service Account User roles assigned at the same time.

iam_sa_no_user_managed_keys.checkTitle: Ensure That There Are Only GCP-Managed Service Account Keys for Each Service Account
iam_sa_no_user_managed_keys.recommendation: It is recommended to prevent user-managed service account keys.

iam_sa_user_managed_key_rotate_90_days.checkTitle: Ensure User-Managed/External Keys for Service Accounts Are Rotated Every 90 Days
iam_sa_user_managed_key_rotate_90_days.recommendation: It is recommended that all Service Account keys are regularly rotated.

iam_sa_user_managed_key_unused.checkTitle: Ensure That There Are No Unused Service Account Keys for Each Service Account
iam_sa_user_managed_key_unused.recommendation: It is recommended to prevent user-managed service account keys.

iam_role_kms_enforce_separation_of_dutie.checkTitle: Enforce Separation of Duties for KMS-Related Roles
iam_role_kms_enforce_separation_of_dutie.recommendation: It is recommended that the principle of 'Separation of Duties' is enforced while assigning KMS related roles to users.

iam_account_access_approval_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Access Approval is Enabled in your account
iam_account_access_approval_enabled.recommendation: Ensure that Access Approval is enabled within your Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account in order to allow you to require your explicit approval whenever Google personnel need to access your GCP projects. Once the Access Approval feature is enabled, you can delegate users within your organization who can approve the access requests by giving them a security role in Identity and Access Management (IAM). These requests show the requester name/ID in an email or Pub/Sub message that you can choose to approve. This creates a new control and logging layer that reveals who in your organization approved/denied access requests to your projects.

iam_no_service_roles_at_project_level.checkTitle: Ensure That IAM Users Are Not Assigned the Service Account User or Service Account Token Creator Roles at Project Level
iam_no_service_roles_at_project_level.recommendation: Ensure that the Service Account User and Service Account Token Creator roles are assigned to a user for a specific GCP service account rather than to a user at the GCP project level, in order to implement the principle of least privilege (POLP). The principle of least privilege (also known as the principle of minimal privilege) is the practice of providing every user the minimal amount of access required to perform its tasks. Google Cloud Platform (GCP) IAM users should not have assigned the Service Account User or Service Account Token Creator roles at the GCP project level. Instead, these roles should be allocated to a user associated with a specific service account, providing that user access to the service account only.

iam_cloud_asset_inventory_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Cloud Asset Inventory Is Enabled
iam_cloud_asset_inventory_enabled.recommendation: Ensure that Cloud Asset Inventory is enabled for all your GCP projects in order to efficiently manage the history and the inventory of your cloud resources. Google Cloud Asset Inventory is a fully managed metadata inventory service that allows you to view, monitor, analyze, and gain insights for your Google Cloud and Anthos assets. Cloud Asset Inventory is disabled by default in each GCP project.

iam_service_account_unused.checkTitle: Ensure That There Are No Unused Service Accounts
iam_service_account_unused.recommendation: It is recommended to disable or remove unused Service Accounts.

iam_organization_essential_contacts_conf.checkTitle: Ensure Essential Contacts is Configured for Organization
iam_organization_essential_contacts_conf.recommendation: It is recommended that Essential Contacts is configured to designate email addresses for Google Cloud services to notify of important technical or security information.

compute_firewall_ssh_access_from_the_int.checkTitle: Ensure That SSH Access Is Restricted From the Internet
compute_firewall_ssh_access_from_the_int.recommendation: Check your Google Cloud Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) firewall rules for inbound rules that allow unrestricted access (i.e. 0.0.0.0/0) on TCP port 22 and restrict the access to trusted IP addresses or IP ranges only in order to implement the principle of least privilege and reduce the attack surface. TCP port 22 is used for secure remote login by connecting an SSH client application with an SSH server. It is strongly recommended to configure your Google Cloud VPC firewall rules to limit inbound traffic on TCP port 22 to known IP addresses only.

compute_project_os_login_2fa_enabled.checkTitle: GCP project has OS Login with 2FA enabled
compute_project_os_login_2fa_enabled.recommendation: Enable OS Login with 2FA at the project level to enforce multi-factor authentication for all SSH connections. This adds a critical security layer by requiring users to complete a second verification step, protecting against credential theft and unauthorized access.
compute_project_os_login_2fa_enabled.other:
1. Navigate to **Compute Engine** > **Metadata** in Google Cloud Console
2. Click **Edit**
3. Add or update metadata entry with key `enable-oslogin-2fa` and value `TRUE`
4. Ensure `enable-oslogin` is also set to `TRUE`
5. Click **Save**

compute_instance_ip_forwarding_is_enable.checkTitle: Ensure That IP Forwarding Is Not Enabled on Instances
compute_instance_ip_forwarding_is_enable.recommendation: Ensure that IP Forwarding feature is not enabled at the Google Compute Engine instance level for security and compliance reasons, as instances with IP Forwarding enabled act as routers/packet forwarders. Because IP forwarding is rarely required, except when the virtual machine (VM) is used as a network virtual appliance, each Google Cloud VM instance should be reviewed in order to decide whether the IP forwarding is really needed for the verified instance. IP Forwarding is enabled at the VM instance level and applies to all network interfaces (NICs) attached to the instance. In addition, Instances created by GKE should be excluded from this recommendation because they need to have IP forwarding enabled and cannot be changed. Instances created by GKE have names that start with "gke- ".

compute_subnet_flow_logs_enabled.checkTitle: Enable VPC Flow Logs for VPC Subnets
compute_subnet_flow_logs_enabled.recommendation: Ensure that VPC Flow Logs is enabled for every subnet created within your production Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network. Flow Logs is a logging feature that enables users to capture information about the IP traffic (accepted, rejected, or all traffic) going to and from the network interfaces (ENIs) available within your VPC subnets.

compute_loadbalancer_logging_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Logging is enabled for HTTP(S) Load Balancer
compute_loadbalancer_logging_enabled.recommendation: Logging will allow you to view HTTPS network traffic to your web applications.

compute_instance_encryption_with_csek_en.checkTitle: Ensure VM Disks for Critical VMs Are Encrypted With Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEK)
compute_instance_encryption_with_csek_en.recommendation: Ensure that the disks attached to your production Google Compute Engine instances are encrypted with Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEKs) in order to have complete control over the data-at-rest encryption and decryption process, and meet strict compliance requirements. These custom keys, also known as Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEKs), are used by Google Compute Engine to protect the Google-generated keys used to encrypt and decrypt your instance data. Compute Engine service does not store your CSEKs on its servers and cannot access your protected data unless you provide the required key.

compute_image_not_publicly_shared.checkTitle: Compute Engine disk image is not publicly shared
compute_image_not_publicly_shared.recommendation: Restrict access to custom disk images by removing the **allAuthenticatedUsers** IAM binding. Apply the principle of least privilege by granting access only to specific users, groups, or service accounts that require it.
compute_image_not_publicly_shared.terraform:
```hcl
resource "google_compute_image_iam_binding" "example_resource" {
  project = "your-project-id"
  image   = "your-image-name"
  role    = "roles/compute.imageUser"
  # Remove allAuthenticatedUsers and grant access only to specific members
  members = [
    "user:specific-user@example.com",
  ]
}
```
compute_image_not_publicly_shared.other:
1. Go to the GCP Console
2. Navigate to Compute Engine > Images
3. Select the disk image
4. Click on the INFO PANEL to view permissions
5. Remove **allAuthenticatedUsers** bindings
6. Click Save

compute_instance_block_project_wide_ssh_.checkTitle: Ensure “Block Project-Wide SSH Keys” Is Enabled for VM Instances
compute_instance_block_project_wide_ssh_.recommendation: It is recommended to use Instance specific SSH keys which can limit the attack surface if the SSH keys are compromised.

compute_instance_group_load_balancer_att.checkTitle: Managed Instance Group is attached to a load balancer
compute_instance_group_load_balancer_att.recommendation: Attach Managed Instance Groups to load balancers using backend services to enable traffic distribution, health checking, and seamless autoscaling. This ensures high availability and optimal performance for production workloads.
compute_instance_group_load_balancer_att.other:
1. Navigate to Network Services > Load balancing
2. Create or edit an HTTP(S) load balancer
3. Configure the backend service
4. Select the target MIG from the instance group dropdown
5. Configure port and balancing mode
6. Complete the load balancer setup

compute_instance_group_multiple_zones.checkTitle: Ensure Managed Instance Groups span multiple zones for high availability
compute_instance_group_multiple_zones.recommendation: Use regional managed instance groups instead of zonal MIGs to distribute instances across multiple zones. This provides automatic failover and load distribution, ensuring high availability for production workloads.
compute_instance_group_multiple_zones.cli: gcloud compute instance-groups managed create INSTANCE_GROUP_NAME --region=REGION --template=INSTANCE_TEMPLATE --size=TARGET_SIZE --zones=ZONE1,ZONE2,ZONE3
compute_instance_group_multiple_zones.terraform:
```hcl
# Create a regional MIG that spans multiple zones
resource "google_compute_region_instance_group_manager" "example" {
  name               = "example-mig"
  region             = "us-central1"
  base_instance_name = "example"
  target_size        = 3

  version {
    instance_template = google_compute_instance_template.example.id
  }

  # Distribute instances across multiple zones
  distribution_policy_zones = ["us-central1-a", "us-central1-b", "us-central1-c"]
}
```
compute_instance_group_multiple_zones.other:
1. Navigate to Compute Engine > Instance groups
2. Click 'Create instance group'
3. Select 'New managed instance group (stateless)'
4. For 'Location', select 'Multiple zones'
5. Choose the target region and zones
6. Configure the instance template and target size
7. Click 'Create'

compute_project_os_login_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Os Login Is Enabled for a Project
compute_project_os_login_enabled.recommendation: Ensure that the OS Login feature is enabled at the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project level in order to provide you with centralized and automated SSH key pair management.

compute_network_not_legacy.checkTitle: Ensure Legacy Networks Do Not Exist
compute_network_not_legacy.recommendation: Ensure that your Google Cloud Platform (GCP) projects are not using legacy networks as this type of network is no longer recommended for production environments because it does not support advanced networking features. Instead, it is strongly recommended to use Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks for existing and future GCP projects.

compute_instance_group_autohealing_enabl.checkTitle: Managed Instance Group has autohealing enabled with a valid health check
compute_instance_group_autohealing_enabl.recommendation: Enable autohealing on all Managed Instance Groups by configuring a health check that validates application-level health. Set an appropriate initial delay to allow instances time to start before health checks begin.
compute_instance_group_autohealing_enabl.cli: gcloud compute instance-groups managed update INSTANCE_GROUP_NAME --health-check=HEALTH_CHECK_NAME --initial-delay=300 --zone=ZONE
compute_instance_group_autohealing_enabl.other:
1. Navigate to Compute Engine > Instance groups
2. Select the Managed Instance Group
3. Click 'Edit'
4. Under 'Autohealing', click 'Add health check'
5. Select or create a health check
6. Set an appropriate initial delay (e.g., 300 seconds)
7. Click 'Save'

compute_network_dns_logging_enabled.checkTitle: Enable Cloud DNS Logging for VPC Networks
compute_network_dns_logging_enabled.recommendation: Cloud DNS logging records the queries from the name servers within your VPC to Stackdriver. Logged queries can come from Compute Engine VMs, GKE containers, or other GCP resources provisioned within the VPC.

compute_instance_single_network_interfac.checkTitle: VM instance has a single network interface
compute_instance_single_network_interfac.recommendation: Configure VM instances with only the **minimum network connectivity** required for their intended purpose. Review instances with multiple network interfaces and consolidate to a single interface unless multi-NIC configuration is explicitly required for network appliance or routing purposes.
compute_instance_single_network_interfac.other:
1. Create a machine image from the non-compliant VM instance
2. Create a new VM instance from the machine image with only one network interface
3. Verify the new instance is functioning correctly
4. Delete the original multi-interface instance

compute_instance_confidential_computing_.checkTitle: Ensure Compute Instances Have Confidential Computing Enabled
compute_instance_confidential_computing_.recommendation: Ensure that the Confidential Computing security feature is enabled for your Google Cloud virtual machine (VM) instances in order to add protection to your sensitive data in use by keeping it encrypted in memory and using encryption keys that Google doesn't have access to. Confidential Computing is a breakthrough technology which encrypts data while it is being processed. This technology keeps data encrypted in memory, outside the CPU.

compute_snapshot_not_outdated.checkTitle: Compute Engine disk snapshot is not outdated
compute_snapshot_not_outdated.recommendation: Implement a snapshot lifecycle policy to automatically delete snapshots older than your organization's retention requirements. Regularly review and clean up outdated snapshots to reduce storage costs and minimize data exposure risks. Consider using scheduled snapshots with automatic deletion policies.
compute_snapshot_not_outdated.other:
1. Open Google Cloud Console and navigate to Compute Engine > Snapshots
2. Identify snapshots older than your retention policy
3. Select outdated snapshots and click **Delete**
4. Confirm the deletion

To automate cleanup, create a snapshot schedule with auto-delete policies under Compute Engine > Snapshots > Snapshot schedules.

compute_instance_preemptible_vm_disabled.checkTitle: VM instance is not configured as preemptible or Spot VM
compute_instance_preemptible_vm_disabled.recommendation: Use standard provisioning model for production and business-critical VM instances. Preemptible and Spot VMs should only be used for fault-tolerant, batch processing, or non-critical workloads that can handle interruptions.
compute_instance_preemptible_vm_disabled.other:
1. Go to Compute Engine console
2. Select the preemptible or Spot VM instance
3. Create a machine image from the instance
4. Create a new instance from the machine image
5. During creation, set **VM provisioning model** to **Standard** (not Spot)
6. Delete the original preemptible or Spot VM instance

compute_instance_disk_auto_delete_disabl.checkTitle: VM instance attached disks have auto-delete disabled
compute_instance_disk_auto_delete_disabl.recommendation: Disable `auto-delete` for all persistent disks attached to **production** and **business-critical** VM instances to prevent **accidental data loss**. Regularly review disk configurations to ensure data retention requirements are met.
compute_instance_disk_auto_delete_disabl.other:
1. Open the Google Cloud Console
2. Navigate to Compute Engine > VM instances
3. Click the target VM instance name
4. Click Edit
5. In the Boot disk section, select 'Keep disk' from the 'When deleting instance' dropdown
6. For Additional disks, click each disk and select 'Keep disk' under 'Deletion rule'
7. Click Save

compute_network_default_in_use.checkTitle: Ensure that the default network does not exist
compute_network_default_in_use.recommendation: When an organization deletes the default network, it may need to migrate or service onto a new network.

compute_instance_serial_ports_in_use.checkTitle: Ensure ‘Enable Connecting to Serial Ports’ Is Not Enabled for VM Instance
compute_instance_serial_ports_in_use.recommendation: Ensure that "Enable connecting to serial ports" configuration setting is disabled for all your production Google Compute Engine instances. A Google Cloud virtual machine (VM) instance has 4 virtual serial ports. On your VM instances, the operating system (OS), BIOS, and other system-level entities write often output data to the serial ports and can accept input, such as commands or answers, to prompts. Usually, these system-level entities use the first serial port (Port 1) and Serial Port 1 is often referred to as the interactive serial console. This interactive serial console does not support IP-based access restrictions such as IP address whitelists. To adhere to cloud security best practices and reduce the risk of unauthorized access, interactive serial console support should be disabled for all instances used in production.

compute_public_address_shodan.checkTitle: Check if any of the Public Addresses are in Shodan (requires Shodan API KEY).
compute_public_address_shodan.recommendation: Check Identified IPs, consider changing them to private ones and delete them from Shodan.

compute_instance_automatic_restart_enabl.checkTitle: Compute Engine VM instances have Automatic Restart enabled
compute_instance_automatic_restart_enabl.recommendation: Enable the Automatic Restart feature for Compute Engine VM instances to enhance system reliability by automatically recovering from crashes or system-initiated terminations. This setting does not interfere with user-initiated shutdowns or stops.
compute_instance_automatic_restart_enabl.other:
1) Open Google Cloud Console → Compute Engine → VM instances
2) Click on the instance name to view details
3) Click 'Edit' at the top of the page
4) Under 'Availability policies', set 'Automatic restart' to 'On (recommended)'
5) Click 'Save' at the bottom of the page

compute_instance_suspended_without_persi.checkTitle: Suspended VM instance does not have persistent disks attached
compute_instance_suspended_without_persi.recommendation: Regularly review suspended VM instances to reduce your attack surface. Either **resume** instances if still needed, or **delete** them along with their attached disks to eliminate potential data exposure. Implement automated policies to detect and alert on long-suspended instances as part of your security monitoring.
compute_instance_suspended_without_persi.other:
1. Open the Google Cloud Console
2. Navigate to Compute Engine > VM instances
3. Identify suspended instances with attached disks
4. If the instance is no longer needed, select it and click DELETE
5. If the instance will be resumed, take no action or resume it with: gcloud compute instances resume INSTANCE_NAME --zone=ZONE

compute_instance_on_host_maintenance_mig.checkTitle: Compute Engine VM instance has On Host Maintenance set to MIGRATE
compute_instance_on_host_maintenance_mig.recommendation: Configure VM instances to use **live migration** during host maintenance events to ensure continuous availability. This is the recommended setting for production workloads that require high availability.
compute_instance_on_host_maintenance_mig.other:
1. Open Google Cloud Console and navigate to Compute Engine > VM instances
2. Click on the instance name to view details
3. Click 'Edit' at the top of the page
4. Under 'Availability policies', set 'On host maintenance' to 'Migrate VM instance (recommended)'
5. Click 'Save' at the bottom of the page

compute_instance_default_service_account.checkTitle: Ensure That Instances Are Not Configured To Use the Default Service Account With Full Access to All Cloud APIs
compute_instance_default_service_account.recommendation: To enforce the principle of least privileges and prevent potential privilege escalation, ensure that your Google Compute Engine instances are not configured to use the default service account with the Cloud API access scope set to "Allow full access to all Cloud APIs". The principle of least privilege (POLP), also known as the principle of least authority, is the security concept of giving the user/system/service the minimal set of permissions required to successfully perform its tasks.

compute_instance_default_service_account.checkTitle: Ensure That Instances Are Not Configured To Use the Default Service Account
compute_instance_default_service_account.recommendation: To defend against privilege escalations if your VM is compromised and prevent an attacker from gaining access to all of your project, it is recommended to not use the default Compute Engine service account. Instead, you should create a new service account and assigning only the permissions needed by your instance. The default Compute Engine service account is named `[PROJECT_NUMBER]-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`.

compute_instance_shielded_vm_enabled.checkTitle: Ensure Compute Instances Are Launched With Shielded VM Enabled
compute_instance_shielded_vm_enabled.recommendation: Ensure that your Google Compute Engine instances are configured to use Shielded VM security feature for protection against rootkits and bootkits.Google Compute Engine service can enable 3 advanced security components for Shielded VM instances: 1. Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM) - this component validates the guest virtual machine (VM) pre-boot and boot integrity, and provides key generation and protection. 2. Integrity Monitoring - lets you monitor and verify the runtime boot integrity of your shielded VM instances using Google Cloud Operations reports (also known as Stackdriver reports). 3. Secure boot helps - this security component protects your VM instances against boot-level and kernel-level malware and rootkits. To defend against advanced threats and ensure that the boot loader and firmware on your Google Compute Engine instances are signed and untampered, it is strongly recommended that your production instances are launched with Shielded VM enabled.

compute_instance_deletion_protection_ena.checkTitle: VM instance has deletion protection enabled
compute_instance_deletion_protection_ena.recommendation: Enable deletion protection on all production and business-critical VM instances to prevent accidental termination. Regularly review instances to ensure critical workloads are protected.
compute_instance_deletion_protection_ena.other:
1. Open the Google Cloud Console
2. Navigate to Compute Engine > VM instances
3. Select the target VM instance
4. Click Edit
5. Under Deletion protection, check the box to enable
6. Click Save

compute_firewall_rdp_access_from_the_int.checkTitle: Ensure That RDP Access Is Restricted From the Internet
compute_firewall_rdp_access_from_the_int.recommendation: Ensure that Google Cloud Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) firewall rules do not allow unrestricted access (i.e. 0.0.0.0/0) on TCP port 3389 in order to restrict Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) traffic to trusted IP addresses or IP ranges only and reduce the attack surface. TCP port 3389 is used for secure remote GUI login to Windows VM instances by connecting a RDP client application with an RDP server.

dns_record_cname_target_valid.checkTitle: DNS records pointing to hostnames have valid targets without takeover risk
dns_record_cname_target_valid.recommendation:
Remove or update **dangling DNS records** to prevent takeover and interception attacks.
- Regularly audit DNS records when decommissioning services
- Remove CNAME, MX, NS, and SRV records pointing to deprovisioned resources
- Monitor for unauthorized changes to DNS records
- Consider using DNS monitoring tools to detect dangling records
dns_record_cname_target_valid.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to DNS > Records
3. Identify CNAME, MX, NS, or SRV records with dangling targets
4. Either update the record to point to a valid target or delete the record
5. If the target service was decommissioned, remove the DNS record

dns_record_no_internal_ip.checkTitle: DNS records do not expose internal IP addresses
dns_record_no_internal_ip.recommendation:
Remove **internal IP addresses** from public DNS records.
- Use split-horizon DNS for internal service resolution
- Ensure DNS records only contain publicly routable IP addresses
- Review DNS records after network changes or migrations
- Consider using Cloudflare Access for secure internal service access
dns_record_no_internal_ip.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to DNS > Records
3. Identify A/AAAA records pointing to internal IP addresses
4. Update records to point to public IP addresses or remove if not needed
5. Use split-horizon DNS if internal resolution is required

dns_record_proxied.checkTitle: Cloudflare proxy is enabled for applicable DNS records
dns_record_proxied.recommendation:
Enable the **Cloudflare proxy** (orange cloud) for DNS records that should be protected.
- Proxied records benefit from DDoS protection, WAF, and caching
- Origin server IP addresses are hidden from public DNS queries
- Apply defense in depth by combining proxy protection with origin hardening
- Some record types (MX, TXT) cannot be proxied by design
dns_record_proxied.terraform:
```hcl
# Enable Cloudflare proxy for DNS records
resource "cloudflare_record" "proxied_record" {
  zone_id = "<ZONE_ID>"
  name    = "www"
  content = "192.0.2.1"
  type    = "A"
  proxied = true # Critical: enables DDoS protection, WAF, and caching
}
```
dns_record_proxied.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to DNS > Records
3. For each A, AAAA, or CNAME record that should be protected
4. Click Edit and toggle Proxy status to Proxied (orange cloud)
5. Save the changes and verify traffic flows through Cloudflare

dns_record_no_wildcard.checkTitle: DNS records do not use wildcard entries
dns_record_no_wildcard.recommendation:
Avoid using **wildcard DNS records** unless absolutely necessary.
- Use specific subdomain records instead of wildcards
- If wildcards are required, ensure the target service handles unknown subdomains securely
- Document the business justification for any wildcard records
- Combine with proper web server configuration to reject unknown hosts
dns_record_no_wildcard.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to DNS > Records
3. Identify wildcard DNS records (starting with *.)
4. Evaluate if the wildcard is necessary for your use case
5. Replace wildcard records with specific subdomain records where possible

zone_browser_integrity_check_enabled.checkTitle: Cloudflare Zone Browser Integrity Check Is Enabled
zone_browser_integrity_check_enabled.recommendation:
Enable **Browser Integrity Check** to filter basic bot traffic.
- Validates HTTP headers to identify non-browser requests
- Challenges requests with missing or invalid browser signatures
- Enabled by default on most Cloudflare plans
- Low impact on legitimate users with standard browsers
zone_browser_integrity_check_enabled.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to Security > Settings
3. Enable Browser Integrity Check
4. This feature is enabled by default on most Cloudflare plans

zone_ssl_strict.checkTitle: SSL/TLS encryption mode is set to Full (Strict)
zone_ssl_strict.recommendation:
Configure **SSL/TLS mode** to `Full (Strict)` and install a valid certificate on your origin server.
- Use **Cloudflare Origin CA certificates** for seamless integration
- Ensure origin server presents a valid certificate matching your domain
- Enable **Authenticated Origin Pulls** for additional security
zone_ssl_strict.terraform:
```hcl
# Set SSL/TLS mode to Full (Strict) for end-to-end encryption
resource "cloudflare_zone_setting" "ssl" {
  zone_id    = "<ZONE_ID>"
  setting_id = "ssl"
  value      = "strict" # Critical: ensures certificate validation between Cloudflare and origin
}
```
zone_ssl_strict.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to SSL/TLS > Overview
3. Under SSL/TLS encryption mode, select Full (strict)
4. Ensure your origin server has a valid SSL certificate installed (Cloudflare Origin CA or publicly trusted CA)

zone_email_obfuscation_enabled.recommendation:
Enable **Email Obfuscation** as part of anti-scraping protections.
- Automatically encodes email addresses to prevent bot harvesting
- Email addresses remain visible and clickable for human visitors
- Works with mailto: links and plain text email addresses
- Part of the Scrape Shield feature set for comprehensive protection
zone_email_obfuscation_enabled.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to Scrape Shield (or Security > Settings in newer UI)
3. Scroll to Email Address Obfuscation
4. Toggle the setting to On
5. Verify that email addresses still work correctly for human visitors

zone_universal_ssl_enabled.recommendation:
Enable **Universal SSL** to provide HTTPS capability for your domain.
- Universal SSL is the foundation for transport security
- Required before implementing HSTS or other HTTPS-dependent features
- Cloudflare automatically renews certificates before expiration
- Consider upgrading to Advanced Certificate Manager for additional control
zone_universal_ssl_enabled.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to SSL/TLS > Edge Certificates
3. Scroll to Universal SSL
4. Ensure the status shows Active
5. If disabled, click Enable Universal SSL
6. Wait for certificate issuance (typically within 24 hours for new domains)

zone_dnssec_enabled.recommendation:
Enable **DNSSEC** and ensure **DS records** are properly configured at your domain registrar.
- DNSSEC provides cryptographic authenticity for DNS responses
- After enabling in Cloudflare, you must add the DS record at your registrar
- Use online DNSSEC validators to verify correct configuration
zone_dnssec_enabled.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to DNS > Settings
3. Scroll to DNSSEC and click Enable DNSSEC
4. Copy the DS record details provided by Cloudflare
5. Add the DS record at your domain registrar
6. Wait for propagation (can take up to 24 hours)

zone_challenge_passage_configured.checkTitle: Cloudflare Zone Challenge Passage Is Configured Between 15 and 45 Minutes
zone_challenge_passage_configured.recommendation:
Configure **Challenge Passage** between 15 and 45 minutes.
- Values below 15 minutes may frustrate legitimate users with excessive challenges
- Values above 45 minutes give attackers too much time after passing challenges
- The default Cloudflare value of 30 minutes is recommended for most use cases
- Adjust based on your specific threat model and user experience requirements
zone_challenge_passage_configured.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to Security > Settings
3. Scroll to Challenge Passage
4. Set the value between 15 and 45 minutes
5. The default value of 30 minutes is recommended for most use cases

zone_automatic_https_rewrites_enabled.recommendation:
Enable **Automatic HTTPS Rewrites** as part of a comprehensive HTTPS strategy.
- Automatically fixes mixed content by rewriting HTTP URLs to HTTPS
- Combine with **Always Use HTTPS** and **HSTS** for defense in depth
- Works best when all resources are available over HTTPS
- Monitor for resources that cannot be rewritten and fix them at the source
zone_automatic_https_rewrites_enabled.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to SSL/TLS > Edge Certificates
3. Scroll to Automatic HTTPS Rewrites
4. Toggle the setting to On
5. Verify that your site loads correctly without mixed content warnings

zone_https_redirect_enabled.recommendation:
Enable **Always Use HTTPS** to enforce encrypted connections for all visitors.
- Combine with **HSTS** to prevent SSL stripping attacks
- Ensure all resources (images, scripts, stylesheets) are served over HTTPS
- Test for mixed content warnings before enabling
zone_https_redirect_enabled.terraform:
```hcl
# Enable Always Use HTTPS to redirect HTTP to HTTPS
resource "cloudflare_zone_setting" "always_use_https" {
  zone_id    = "<ZONE_ID>"
  setting_id = "always_use_https"
  value      = "on" # Critical: forces all traffic to use encrypted HTTPS
}
```
zone_https_redirect_enabled.other:
1. Log in to the Cloudflare dashboard and select your account and domain
2. Go to SSL/TLS > Edge Certificates
3. Scroll to Always Use HTTPS
4. Toggle the setting to On
5. Verify that your site works correctly over HTTPS
